info.title: picweight API
info.description: AI-assisted calorie & БЖУ tracker. Photograph what you eat; a server-side estimation agent returns calories and macros.

get.description: Verifies the CSRF token against the state cookie, exchanges the authorization code with the PKCE verifier, validates the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, signature), upserts the `users` row and sets the `picweight_session` cookie.

302.description: Redirect to the app with a session cookie set

get.description: Issuer, client ids and scopes, so the Android app and the SPA only need to be told the picweight server URL.

Starts the authorization-code + PKCE flow for the confidential web client. The PKCE verifier, nonce and CSRF token are stored in a short-lived signed cookie so the callback needs no server-side session store.
Clears the `picweight_session` cookie and redirects to the login page. Bearer-token clients simply discard their token; nothing is stored server-side.
Returns the claims of the presented session JWT without touching the database or the IdP. Use `GET /api/v1/me` for the profile and today's targets.

post.description: Accepts a currently-valid session (bearer header or cookie) and issues a new JWT with a fresh expiry. An expired session cannot be resurrected — that path is a full re-login. Cookie callers also get the cookie re-set.

post.summary: Exchange an OIDC ID token for a session JWT
post.description: The Android app runs authorization-code + PKCE against the **native (public)** client itself, then posts the resulting ID token here. The token is verified against the provider's JWKS — accepted for either the web or the mobile client id — and a picweight session JWT is returned for use as `Authorization: Bearer`.

post.summary: Resolve a barcode to a food record
post.description: Reads the local `foods` cache first, then Open Food Facts. `POST` rather than `GET` because a miss performs an outbound fetch and writes the cache.

get.summary: Get a day's totals and remaining budget

parameters.name: tz_offset
parameters.description:
Minutes east of UTC to bucket by. Defaults to the offset of the user's
most recent meal, then to the profile timezone.

get.description: Powers the capture screen's recent-dish chips — one tap sets the dish name, no keyboard. Confirmed meals only.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many chips to return. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_RECENT_LIMIT`], capped at
[`MAX_RECENT_LIMIT`].

get.description: Member meals plus combined totals. Each meal was analysed by its own independent loop and stays independently correctable.

404.description: No such group for this user

get.summary: Current user, profile and today's state

put.summary: Update body data and recompute targets
put.description: Targets are computed with Mifflin-St Jeor — deterministic, offline and auditable. A deficit steeper than ~1% bodyweight/week is returned as a warning, not an error.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum meals to return. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_HISTORY_LIMIT`].

post.description: Multipart ingest. Idempotent on `client_uuid`: replaying the same key returns the existing meal with `deduplicated: true` rather than creating a duplicate. Returns 202 — analysis is always asynchronous.

get.description: Server-sent events for this user only. Each `completed`, `reanalyzed` and `group_settled` event carries the full day state so a client can render the notification without a follow-up request.

200.description: text/event-stream; each frame is a JSON MealEvent under the `meal` event name

404.description: No such meal for this user
No such meal for this user

patch.description: Confirming a meal is what feeds `recall_similar_meals` — only confirmed meals, latest revision, are ever recalled. Every changed field is recorded in `item_corrections`.

404.description: No such meal for this user

post.description: Loads the persisted rig thread, appends the feedback as a new user turn and continues the same conversation, emitting a new revision. Prior revisions are retained. Returns 202 — the correction runs in the background.

404.description: No such meal for this user

409.description: An analysis is already running for this meal

404.description: No such meal for this user

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum readings to return. Defaults to [`DEFAULT_WEIGHT_LIMIT`].

post.description: Recomputes the user's targets from the new weight, since targets are derived from body data and must track it.

get.description:
Deliberately does *not* touch the database: a probe that fails because
SQLite is briefly locked would restart a pod that is merely busy.

AuthConfigResponse.description: OIDC settings a client needs so it only has to be told the server URL.

mobile_client_id.description: Public/native client id for the Android app, when configured.

CreateMealForm.description:
The multipart form accepted by `POST /api/v1/meals`.

Declared for the OpenAPI spec; the handler reads the parts directly because
axum's `Multipart` is a stream.

client_uuid.description: Idempotency key generated on the phone at capture. Required.

dish_name.description: Dish name from a chip, share intent, or comment.

eaten_at.description: When the meal was eaten, RFC 3339.

group_size.description:
How many photos the sitting will contain; settles the group instantly
once all N are terminal.

photo.description: The photo. Optional — a manual entry has none (§5 "Manual entry").

timezone_offset.description: Minutes east of UTC at capture.

DayResponse.description: Totals, targets, remaining and the verdict line for one local day.

meals.description: Meals not belonging to any sitting, newest first.

state.description: The rules-engine state: consumed, targets, remaining, classification.

verdict.description: One line of plain-language advice, templated or LLM-phrased.

DayState.description:
A day's totals against its targets.

Carried verbatim in the `/meals/events` completion payload so a client
renders the notification from one message with no follow-up round trip (§9).

date.description: The local calendar day these figures cover.

meals_logged.description: Meals logged on this day (all statuses except `failed`).

remaining_protein_g.description: Protein still owed, grams; clamped at zero.

status.description: Classification derived from the figures above.

target_kcal.description: Energy target, kcal. Zero when targets are not computed.

DayStatus.description: How a day is going. Computed from the numbers, never asked of a model.

ErrorBody.description: The JSON body returned for every [`AppError`].

message.description: Human-readable detail. Generic for 5xx, specific for 4xx.

EstimatedItem.description: One component of a dish: the rice, the sauce, the chicken.

barcode.description: EAN, when the item was resolved from a barcode.

grams.description: Estimated edible mass in grams. This is where nearly all the error lives.

kcal.description: Energy for the stated grams (not per 100g).

reasoning_note.description:
One line of "why", shown next to the item so the user can see the
reasoning without opening the inspector (§5, step 5).

export_version.description: Schema version of this document, so an importer can adapt.

meals.description: Every meal at its current revision.

oneOf.description: Body data and targets, when onboarding is complete.

FoodFacts.description: Normalized per-100g nutrition for one packaged product.

barcode.description: The barcode this record was resolved from.

brand.description: Brand, when the provider knows one.

source_ref.description: Provider-side identifier — the barcode, for Open Food Facts.

fetched_at.description: When the record was last fetched from the provider.

GramsSource.description: Where an item's gram figure came from.

GroupResponse.description: One sitting: its member meals and their combined totals.

expected_size.description: The client's `group_size` hint, when it sent one.

last_photo_at.description: When the most recent photo joined; the debounce runs from here.

meals.description: The member meals, oldest first — the expanded per-dish rows.

notified_at.description: When the single grouped notification fired, if it has.

settled.description: True once no member is still `pending` or `analyzing`.

GroupSummary.description: A group as it appears collapsed in the day view.

dish_names.description: Dish names, for the collapsed row's label.

has_failures.description:
True when a member failed — the row should say so rather than quietly
under-report.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the process is serving.

logged_at.description: When it was measured. Defaults to now.

oneOf.description: How it was captured. Defaults to `manual`.

targets_recomputed.description: True when this reading caused targets to be recomputed.

MacroSource.description: Where an item's macros came from.

MacroTotals.description: Summed macros, used for meals, days and groups alike.

oneOf.description: Body data and targets. `None` until onboarding completes.

today.description: Today's state, so the home screen renders from one request.

version.description: Backend version string, for the about screen and drift diagnosis.

MealAcceptedResponse.description: 202 body returned by ingest and by re-analysis.

deduplicated.description:
True when an existing meal was returned because `client_uuid` had
already been seen — the idempotent-replay path.

meal_id.description: The meal that was created or resumed.

revision.description: Revision the enqueued job will write.

status.description:
Always `pending` for a new upload; the revision being produced for a
re-analysis.

MealEstimate.description: What the agent returns for one photo.

container.description:
The container identified in the frame — a standard delivery bowl, a 30cm
pizza box, a 0.5L cup. With no comment and no coin on the plate this is
the only reliable scale reference, so the prompt pushes hard on it (§5).

cuisine.description: Cuisine, when it is a useful prior (e.g. "Thai", "Georgian").

dish_name.description:
The dish as identified (or as supplied by the user, which outranks the
visual read).

from_recall.description:
Whether the estimate came from the user's own confirmed history.
Surfaced at confirm time so "this came from your history" is visible
rather than implicit (PRD §14.1).

notes.description: Free-form note about the estimate as a whole.

MealEvent.description:
One event on the stream.

`Clone` because broadcast hands every subscriber its own copy.

body.description: Line 2 + 3 + 4 of the notification, already phrased.

oneOf.description: The day state, so no follow-up request is needed.

dish_name.description: Dish name — the notification leads with it (§6).

emitted_at.description: When the event was produced, UTC.

group_id.description: The sitting, when the meal belongs to one.

oneOf.description: Totals for the meal, or for the whole sitting on `GroupSettled`.

MealFeedback.description:
A self-contained notification payload.

Self-contained is the requirement, not a nicety: the notification fires
~20–30s after capture, by which time the phone may be pocketed, so it has to
make sense read cold minutes later. Lead with the dish name (§6 timing).

day.description:
The full day state, so a client renders from one message with no
follow-up round trip.

headline.description: Line 1 — what was logged: "Шаурма с курицей — 780 kcal".

macro_status.description: Line 3 — macro status against the floor that actually binds.

standing.description: Line 2 — where you stand: "1,450 / 2,050 today · 600 left".

verdict.description:
Line 4 — the one-line verdict, LLM-phrased from the numbers with a
templated fallback.

barcode.description: EAN, when resolved from a barcode.

reasoning_note.description: One line of "why", shown next to the item.

MealResponse.description: A meal with its items at the current revision.

error.description: Failure reason when `status` is `failed` — visible, never silent (§5).

group_id.description: The sitting this meal belongs to, if any.

group_size.description: Client hint for how many photos the sitting will contain.

name_source.description: Which input path supplied the name — instrumented per §14.2.

portion_scale.description: "Ate 60% of it" multiplier; already applied to `items` and `totals`.

thumbnail_url.description: Relative URL of the 768px thumbnail, or `None` for a manual entry.

timezone_offset.description: Minutes east of UTC at capture; buckets the local day.

user_comment.description: The user's comment, when they typed one.

MealStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a meal. `pending`/`analyzing` are in-flight, `needs_review`
means the agent produced a draft the user has not confirmed, `confirmed`
is the only status `recall_similar_meals` reads from, `failed` is loud.

NameSource.description:
Which input path supplied the dish name. Instrumented in M4 to answer
PRD §14.2 — whether the zero-keyboard paths actually get used.

barcode.description: EAN, when the user scanned one.

id.description: Existing `meal_items.id`, or omitted to add a new item.

PatchMealRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /api/v1/meals/:id` — confirm, or edit items.

items.description:
Full replacement item list. Omit to leave items untouched.

Every changed field is written to `item_corrections` so the correction
history — and the per-user `calibration_factor` derived from it — stays
complete.

oneOf.description: New status. Only `confirmed` is meaningful from a client.

ProfileResponse.description: Body data and the targets derived from it.

calibration_factor.description: Per-user multiplier learned from correction history (§5 hidden fat).

current_weight_kg.description: Most recent logged weight, for convenience.

sex.description: Biological sex — changes the BMR constant by 166 kcal.

targets_computed_at.description: When the targets were last recomputed.

timezone.description: IANA timezone name, the default for meals that arrive without an offset.

feedback.description:
What is wrong, in the user's words: "too much rice, it was about half
that". Stored verbatim on `analysis_jobs.user_feedback` — it is far
richer signal than a gram delta.

RecentDish.description: One previously confirmed dish, ready to become a chip.

dish_name.description: The dish name as the user confirmed it.

dish_name_normalized.description: Normalized form — what recall matches on.

last_eaten_at.description: Most recent time this dish was eaten.

last_meal_id.description: The meal those totals came from, for a "same as last time" shortcut.

occurrences.description:
How many times it has been confirmed. High counts are the flywheel
working.

totals.description:
Totals from the most recent confirmed occurrence, so the chip can show
"≈780 kcal".

RevisionEntry.description: One entry of a meal's revision history.

reseeded.description: Whether the session was continued or reseeded.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls made producing it. Zero on a continuation is the point (§13).

user_feedback.description: The verbatim feedback that caused this revision, if any.

SessionClaims.description: Claims carried by a picweight session JWT.

email.description: Email from the ID token, or empty.

iss.description: Issuer URL the subject came from.

name.description: Display name from the ID token, or empty.

sub.description: OIDC subject — stable per user per issuer.

Sex.description: Biological sex, as required by the Mifflin-St Jeor BMR formula (§6).

age_years.description: Age in years at the time of computation.

rate_kg_per_week.description:
Intended rate of change in kg per week (always positive; direction comes
from `goal_type`).

sex.description: Biological sex — the BMR constant differs by 166 kcal.

target_weight_kg.description: Target weight in kilograms; drives the protein and fat floors.

id_token.description: ID token obtained by the native client from the IdP.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Body of `PUT /api/v1/me/profile`.

This is the onboarding payload and the edit payload both; every field is
required because the formulas need all of them.

current_weight_kg.description:
Current weight. When present, also written to `weight_logs` with source
`onboarding`, since targets recompute on weight change (G6).

rate_kg_per_week.description: Intended rate of change, kg/week (always positive).

profile.description: The saved profile with freshly computed targets.

warnings.description:
Non-fatal advice — e.g. an aggressive deficit. Warned about, not
silently accepted (§6).

created_at.description: When the account was first seen.

display_name.description: Display name from the ID token.

email.description: Email from the ID token, when the IdP supplied one.

WeightSource.description: How a weight reading was captured.

session.description: Session JWT. Web clients receive it as the HttpOnly `picweight_session` cookie after OIDC login; native clients obtain it from `POST /api/auth/token` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer`.
